transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Navarro, Priya Shah, Tomas Reed (Redwood); Jordan Lee, Maya Patel, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Ruiz (Greenridge)
Links shared: SOC2 PDF (link: https://redwood.example/soc2/gr-2026), Trust Portal invite (sent), Encryption WhtPpr (link)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick rolodex, I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the account, Priya is our SE, Tomas is on CS. Jordan, Maya, Liam, Sofia from Greenridge, got it?
[00:18] Jordan (Greenridge): Yep hi all, thanks. We're mostly here to understand what artifacts you have available and how we can onboard our auditors to the portal. We have an audit window late July.
[00:28] Maya (Greenridge): And want to confirm the RBAC model and how Trust Portal access maps to our internal roles — we can't give full access to contractors etc.
[00:36] Priya (Redwood): Totally, that's exactly what we'll walk through. High level: we provide SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO artifacts optionally, and a Trust Portal where you can invite users and assign roles. The portal supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:50] Liam (Greenridge): SCIM is important for us, yes. Also KMS — do you support customer-managed keys or only Redwood-managed? We have residency constraints and key separation requirements.
[01:05] Priya: Good question. For hosted deployments we offer both Redwood-managed with KMS integration and customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) patterns. For Private/VPC there is an option to host the control plane in your VPC and integrate with your HSM or cloud KMS. There are a couple of permutations — we'll need a follow-up tech deep-dive to map to your infra.
[01:25] Sofia (Greenridge): When you say BYOK, does Redwood ever have the key material? We need to be sure there's separation.
[01:33] Priya: No, with BYOK the key material is under your KMS control. Redwood negotiates access to decrypt for ephemeral inference, but the key lifecycle (rotation, revocation) is in your KMS. For on-prem HSM integration we can provide an ops guide. There might be some subtlety around backup keys, we'll detail that in the deep-dive.
[01:52] Jordan: Ok. About audit logs — we need to export logs into our SIEM and retain for 2 years per policy. What does Redwood provide in terms of log schema and retention?
[02:03] Alex: We surface request-level audit logs, admin actions, and key events. By default logs are retained for 90 days in hosted plans, with add-on retention packages for longer. For Dedicated/Private you can configure export to your S3 or syslog endpoint. Priya, correct me on schema details?
[02:17] Priya: Schema includes timestamp, request id, user id, model id, route, bytes in/out, latency, and action type (e.g., admin:create-user). We can provide a sample export, and push-to-s3 or direct syslog/HTTP ingest into your SIEM. There are some anonymization rules we apply by default to PII — we can toggle fields depending on agreement.
[02:36] Maya: Great — the anonymization is fine but we'll need full admin action logs for compliance. Also want to confirm who in Redwood gets access to customer logs for support.
[02:45] Priya: Support level access is gated. For hosteds with support we have privileged support roles, access is logged and requires approval; for Dedicated/Private we don't need to access your logs unless you enable a support bundle. All access is tracked in the Trust Portal.
[03:02] Liam: You mentioned Trust Portal roles — what roles exist? We need least privilege for auditors vs ops vs devs.
[03:09] Alex: Default roles are Admin, Auditor, Developer, Read-only Ops. Auditor role can view reports and download evidence bundles but cannot change config. We also support custom roles and can scope SSO groups to roles via SAML assertions.
[03:24] Jordan: Is there RBAC at the model level? We have internal models with restricted access.
[03:31] Priya: Yes, we support per-model access controls via policies. You can tag models and assign team-level permissions, and we integrate with your IdP groups for automatic mapping.
[03:45] Sofia: For the Trust Portal, can audit logs be exported per user activity?
[03:49] Priya: Yes. We can run activity exports filtered by user, org unit, or timeframe. There is a caveat: very granular exports for very large orgs can be heavy — we'll scope the exports in the tech call.
[04:05] Maya: On SOC 2 — do you provide the full bridge letter and any carve-outs? Our auditors will want to see the exception testing windows.
[04:13] Alex: We provide the SOC 2 Type II report and a cover letter. Any carve-outs are called out in the report. We'll share the redacted report now, and if your auditors need direct access to the unredacted under NDA we can coordinate that via the Trust Portal permissions.
[04:30] Liam: Timeline wise, if our audit window is late July, when should we finalize evidence handoff?
[04:37] Alex: Ideally you grant Trust Portal auditor access by early July and we provide a tailored evidence bundle two weeks before the window. So plan for July 10th - 15th for evidence snapshot.
[04:54] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. What about encryption in transit and at rest — any specifics about algorithms, ephemeral keys, or TLS termination?
[05:02] Priya: In-flight is TLS 1.2+ ; at-rest we use AES-256. For customer-managed KMS we leverage your envelope encryption where Redwood stores only wrapped keys. If you need FIPS-validated HSMs for key ops, we support that in Private deployments.
[05:22] Sofia: Do you support key rotation policies enforced by us? We need rotation every 90 days for certain keys.
[05:29] Priya: Yes, you can enforce rotation on your KMS side. Redwood will pick up rotated keys as long as the key alias remains valid; for asymmetric flows there's a short rollover choreography we'll document.
[05:41] Maya: Data residency — our EU customers must keep logs in EU. Does Redwood offer region-scoped log retention and model hosting?
[05:49] Alex: Yes, we have region-aware hosting. You can pin inference to EU regions and route logs to EU S3 or your VPC. For Hosted we have EU regions; for Dedicated/Private you can run in your VPC/region. We'll show the routing policy options in the deep-dive.
[06:04] Jordan: On legal — do you provide subprocessing lists and DPA?
[06:08] Alex: Yes, we have a standard DPA and subprocessors list; I'll attach both.
[06:12] Liam: Can you walk through a hypothetical evidence package? What would auditors expect to see?
[06:18] Priya: Typical package: SOC2 report, system descriptions, user access lists at snapshot time, change control records, key rotation logs, admin action logs, and sample infra diagrams. We can create a curated bundle per your auditor's checklist.
[06:33] Maya: For the admin action logs, are they tamper-evident? We need integrity proofs.
[06:38] Priya: We use write-once storage for audit entries in the hosted offering and provide hash chains for tamper-evidence on request. We'll include the mechanism in the whitepaper.
[06:50] Jordan: Ok, next steps then?
[06:53] Alex: I'll share the SOC2 redacted PDF and Trust Portal invite shortly after this call. Priya will coordinate a technical deep-dive focused on KMS and log exports; can we tentatively lock the week of June 8th?
[07:05] Maya: That works. Also we'll send the list of auditors and any restricted IP ranges we need respected.
[07:11] Sofia: And I'll put together an infra diagram.
[07:15] Liam: Could Redwood run a small demo of the Trust Portal to show the auditor role and evidence download flow?
[07:21] Tomas (Redwood): Sure, we can do a 20-30 minute walk-through during the tech deep-dive or as a separate session if you prefer.
[07:31] Jordan: Let's include it in the tech deep-dive.
[07:34] Alex: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:36] Maya: One quick question — for support, if we need Redwood to assist with evidence collection, what's the SLA and cost?
[07:42] Alex: For enterprise customers, premium support includes evidence collection assistance and faster response SLAs. We'll include pricing in the follow-up email.
[07:50] Jordan: Good. Thanks everyone.
[07:52] Alex: Thanks all — recap in the follow-up email, action items and links.
[07:58] End of call.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker overlap, some technical terms mis-typed (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache), minor audio cut near 00:36 resulting in a short gap.
